title: Browser testing and issue reporting
learningObjectives: Complete browser testing and issue reporting using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Browser testing checks real user workflows across relevant browsers, viewport sizes, input methods, and network conditions. A useful issue report includes environment, reproduction steps, expected and actual behaviour, and safe evidence.
understand.whyItMatters: A site can pass code checks yet fail during real interaction. Reproducible reports make debugging and prioritisation faster.
understand.analogy: Browser testing is a rehearsal of the user's actual journey rather than inspection of the script alone.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The object models a reproducible issue report. Replace placeholders with real observations and remove private information.

examples.code: const issue={environment:'Browser/version/device',steps:['Open course','Open lesson','Run practice'],expected:'Preview updates',actual:'Preview remains blank'};console.log(issue);
examples.explanation: The object models a reproducible issue report. Replace placeholders with real observations and remove private information.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Test the capstone in at least two browsers and multiple viewport sizes. Record defects with exact reproduction steps and evidence.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
